title: 宣德元年福建鄉試錄
text:
大賢言聖德之盛同乎造化之妙復即天地之道以明聖德之大夫聖人
之德未易言也苟不即天地造化之道以明之又何以見聖德之所以為大
乎今夫夫子之德廣博深厚而天下之道無一之不該非如地之博厚載華
岳而不重振河海而不洩者乎夫子之德高大光明而天下之理無一之或
遺豈不猶天之高明日月星辰繫焉萬物覆焉者乎持載如地聖人博厚
之至也覆幬如天聖人高明之至也至於仕止久速之各當其可則與春夏秋
冬之迭運者無或殊仁義禮智之時出者則與日月代明乎晝夜者無以異
錯行如四時代明如日月此聖人悠久之至也然以造化喻聖人固足以見聖
德之大不即天地之大又何以見聖德之所以為大乎是故天覆地載飛潜
===
蠢動各正性命此萬物之並育未嘗或相害也四時日月錯行代明循
環無巳此道之並行未嘗或相悖也所以不害不悖者小德之川流所
以並育並行者大德之敦化小德者全體之分大德者萬殊之本川
流者如川之流脉絡分明而往不息萬物各具一太極也敦化者敦
厚其化根本盛大而出無窮萬物統體一太極也此天地之所以為
大也知天地之大則聖人之為大可知觀其渾然一理四端五典無不統於
其間則與並育並行者同一機泛應曲當萬物萬事莫不由是而行
則與不害不悖者無二致泛應曲當亦小德之川流一理渾然亦大德之
敦化也吁大哉天地之道乎至哉聖人之德乎非天地之道固不足以明聖
punctuated: 大賢言聖德之盛同乎造化之妙，復即天地之道以明聖德之大。夫聖人之德，未易言也；苟不即天地造化之道以明之，又何以見聖德之所以為大乎？今夫夫子之德，廣博深厚，而天下之道無一之不該，非如地之博厚，載華岳而不重，振河海而不洩者乎？夫子之德，高大光明，而天下之理無一之或遺，豈不猶天之高明，日月星辰繫焉，萬物覆焉者乎？持載如地，聖人博厚之至也；覆幬如天，聖人高明之至也。至於仕止久速之各當其可，則與春夏秋冬之迭運者無或殊；仁義禮智之時出者，則與日月代明乎晝夜者無以異。錯行如四時，代明如日月，此聖人悠久之至也。然以造化喻聖人，固足以見聖德之大；不即天地之大，又何以見聖德之所以為大乎？是故天覆地載，飛潜蠢動各正性命，此萬物之並育，未嘗或相害也；四時日月，錯行代明，循環無巳，此道之並行，未嘗或相悖也。所以不害不悖者，小德之川流；所以並育並行者，大德之敦化。小德者，全體之分；大德者，萬殊之本。川流者，如川之流，脉絡分明而往不息，萬物各具一太極也；敦化者，敦厚其化，根本盛大而出無窮，萬物統體一太極也。此天地之所以為大也。知天地之大，則聖人之為大可知。觀其渾然一理，四端五典無不統於其間，則與並育並行者同一機；泛應曲當，萬物萬事莫不由是而行，則與不害不悖者無二致。泛應曲當，亦小德之川流；一理渾然，亦大德之敦化也。吁！大哉天地之道乎！至哉聖人之德乎！非天地之道，固不足以明聖
translation_en: The great worthy speaks of the flourishing of the sage's virtue as identical to the subtlety of the creative transformation of nature, and further draws upon the Way of Heaven and Earth to illuminate the greatness of the sage's virtue. Now, the virtue of the sage is not easily put into words; if one does not draw upon the Way of Heaven and Earth and their creative transformation to illuminate it, how else could one see why the sage's virtue is great? Now, the virtue of the Master [Confucius] is vast, broad, deep, and thick, and there is not a single aspect of the Way under heaven that it does not encompass—is it not like the breadth and thickness of Earth, which supports Mount Hua and the other sacred peaks without feeling their weight, and contains the rivers and seas without letting them leak away? The virtue of the Master is lofty, great, bright, and shining, and there is not a single principle under heaven that it leaves out—is it not like the loftiness and brightness of Heaven, from which the sun, moon, and stars are suspended, and by which the myriad things are sheltered? Supporting and bearing like the Earth is the utmost of the sage's breadth and thickness; sheltering and covering like Heaven is the utmost of the sage's loftiness and brightness. As for serving or retiring, tarrying or hastening, each fitting what is proper, this is no different from the alternating revolutions of spring, summer, autumn, and winter; and humanity, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom emerging at their proper times are no different from the sun and moon alternating their brightness through day and night. Alternating in their courses like the four seasons and alternating in brightness like the sun and moon—this is the utmost of the sage's enduring permanence. Yet while comparing the sage to creative transformation is indeed sufficient to show the greatness of the sage's virtue, without drawing upon the greatness of Heaven and Earth themselves, how could one see why the sage's virtue is great? Therefore, as Heaven covers and Earth bears, flying, submerged, and wriggling creatures each attain their proper nature and destiny—this is the myriad things being nourished together without ever harming one another. The four seasons and the sun and moon alternate in their courses and alternate in brightness, revolving in an endless cycle—this is their courses proceeding together without ever coming into conflict. That by which they do not harm or conflict with one another is the lesser virtues flowing like river currents; that by which they are nourished together and proceed together is the great virtue thickening transformation. The lesser virtues are the differentiations of the whole body; the great virtue is the root of the myriad differences. "Flowing like river currents" means that like the flowing of rivers, the veins and channels are distinct and go on without ceasing, each of the myriad things possessing its own Supreme Ultimate (Taiji); "thickening transformation" means making its transformations thick and substantial, the root and foundation being grand and abundant and issuing forth inexhaustibly, the myriad things collectively embodying a single Supreme Ultimate. This is why Heaven and Earth are great. Knowing the greatness of Heaven and Earth, one can know the greatness of the sage. Observing how within his undifferentiated single principle, the Four Beginnings and Five Canonized Relationships are all encompassed without exception, this shares the same vital mechanism as things being nourished together and proceeding together; and in his responding broadly and fitting every particular curve, so that among the myriad things and myriad affairs there is none that does not proceed from this, this is no different from their neither harming nor conflicting with one another. Responding broadly and fitting every particular is likewise the lesser virtues flowing like river currents; the single principle undifferentiated is likewise the great virtue thickening transformation. Ah! Great indeed is the Way of Heaven and Earth! Utmost indeed is the virtue of the sage! Without the Way of Heaven and Earth, it would indeed be insufficient to illuminate the sage's…

title: 宣德元年福建鄉試錄
text:
於我公舍爵策勳之日特書曰公至自夾谷豈非禮以服大國春秋托望國
之至以著其美乎雖然以一時之事功而論則其美或可以並稱以春秋之大法
律之則伯者之功豈可與聖人之化同日而語哉自夫伐楚之後召陵還師
而肆侵陳之忿葵丘震矜而致九國之叛則齊桓雖有其功不能無其過
矣自夫夾谷之後三田來歸既有得齊人之歸心墮郈墮費復有以致三
家之效順則聖人不唯能變齊而又能變魯矣吁伯者之功過不相掩不足
論也惜夫女樂魯庭聖轍汶上吾夫子之心不得直遂於魯可勝嘆哉
禮記
是故聖人之記事也慮之以大愛之以敬行之以禮脩之以孝養
===
紀之以義終之以仁是故古之人一舉事而衆皆知其德之
備也〔十三名洪顯〕
同考試官訓導柴批〔禮經三篇經旨貫徹組織不凡此篇他卷破題於古人一舉處不能包括獨此一破尤妙中〕
〔間講新節詳整無隙可議真佳作也四書二篇皆得其旨後場論策善發明條答尤宜〕
〔前列〕
考試官教諭邵批〔此篇理明文贍可爲程式三場俱優一薦何忝〕
考試官前侍講余批〔四書本經皆詳明此篇破題以篤近舉遠由此達彼爲一篇之関鍵傑然超於他作後塲〕
〔論策皆平順宜在前列〕
觀聖人之記大事篤近而舉遠者其義爲甚詳則知古人之舉大事由此
punctuated:
於我公舍爵策勳之日，特書曰：「公至自夾谷。」豈非禮以服大國，《春秋》托望國之至以著其美乎？雖然，以一時之事功而論，則其美或可以並稱；以《春秋》之大法律之，則伯者之功豈可與聖人之化同日而語哉？自夫伐楚之後，召陵還師而肆侵陳之忿，葵丘震矜而致九國之叛，則齊桓雖有其功，不能無其過矣。自夫夾谷之後，三田來歸，既有得齊人之歸心；墮郈、墮費，復有以致三家之效順，則聖人不唯能變齊，而又能變魯矣。吁！伯者之功過不相掩，不足論也；惜夫女樂魯庭，聖轍汶上，吾夫子之心不得直遂於魯，可勝嘆哉！

《禮記》

是故聖人之記事也，慮之以大，愛之以敬，行之以禮，脩之以孝養，紀之以義，終之以仁。是故古之人一舉事，而衆皆知其德之備也。〔十三名洪顯〕

同考試官訓導柴批：〔《禮》經三篇，經旨貫徹，組織不凡。此篇他卷破題於古人一舉處不能包括，獨此一破尤妙。中間講新節詳整，無隙可議，真佳作也。《四書》二篇皆得其旨，後場論、策善發明，條答尤宜前列。〕
考試官教諭邵批：〔此篇理明文贍，可爲程式。三場俱優，一薦何忝。〕
考試官前侍講余批：〔《四書》、本經皆詳明。此篇破題以「篤近舉遠，由此達彼」爲一篇之関鍵，傑然超於他作。後塲論、策皆平順，宜在前列。〕

觀聖人之記大事，篤近而舉遠者，其義爲甚詳；則知古人之舉大事，由此…
translation_en:
…on the day our Duke drank the cup in the ancestral temple and recorded the merits, specially wrote: "The Duke arrived from Jiagu." Is this not because ritual propriety was used to win over a great state, and the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) relied on the record of the Duke's return from an anxiously awaited journey to highlight its excellence? Even so, if discussed in terms of the achievements of a single moment, their merits might perhaps be mentioned together; yet if judged by the great standard of the Spring and Autumn Annals, how could the achievements of a hegemon be spoken of on the same day as the transformative influence of a sage? After the campaign against Chu, upon withdrawing his army from Shaoling he gave rein to his anger by invading Chen, and at Kuiqiu his arrogant pride provoked the rebellion of nine states; thus although Duke Huan of Qi had his achievements, he was not without his faults. After the meeting at Jiagu, the lands of the three cities were returned, which already won the allegiance of the people of Qi; and the dismantling of the walls of Hou and Bi further brought the Three Families to submit in obedience—thus the Sage was able not only to transform Qi, but also to transform Lu. Alas! The achievements and faults of a hegemon do not cancel each other out and are not worth discussing; how regrettable that when the female musicians were received in the court of Lu and the Sage's carriage tracks turned toward the Wen River, the aspiration of our Master could not be directly fulfilled in Lu—how can one sigh enough over this!

Record of Rites (Liji)

"Therefore, when the sages recorded events, they planned them on a grand scale, loved with reverence, carried them out with ritual propriety, cultivated them with filial nourishment, regulated them with righteousness, and concluded them with benevolence. Therefore, when the ancients undertook a single affair, everyone knew that their virtue was complete." [13th place, Hong Xian 洪顯]

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Chai 柴: ["In the three essays on the Classic of Rites, the meaning of the classic is thoroughly penetrated and the structure is extraordinary. On this topic, the opening statements (poti) of other papers failed to encompass the part about the ancients undertaking a single affair, whereas this opening alone is especially marvelous. The middle sections expounding the subdivisions are detailed, orderly, and beyond reproach—truly a fine piece. Two of the Four Books essays grasp the essential meaning, and in the later sessions the discourse and policy essays are well-developed, with the itemized responses especially worthy of the front ranks."]
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Shao 邵: ["In this essay the principles are clear and the writing is rich; it can serve as a model answer. All three sessions are excellent—what shame could there be in recommending him?"]
Comment by Examiner and former Expositor-in-waiting Yu 余: ["Both the Four Books and the candidate's specialized classic essays are detailed and clear. The opening statement of this essay takes 'devoting oneself to what is near and raising up what is distant, reaching from this to that' as the key to the whole piece, standing out far above the other compositions. The discourse and policy essays of the later sessions are all smooth and well-reasoned; he deserves to be placed in the front ranks."]

When we observe that in the sages' recording of great affairs—devoting themselves to what is near and raising up what is distant—their principles are exceedingly detailed, we know that when the ancients undertook great affairs, reaching from this…

title: 宣德元年福建鄉試錄
text:
而達彼者其德無不該夫養老之禮王道之大端也今也聖人篤近以舉遠者
其義無不詳則其推此而達彼者其德又豈有不該者哉記禮者知其然謂
夫虞夏商周皆有養老之禮後王亦皆記序前代之事也然天子莫重於養
老人道莫大於孝弟養老之禮無非謀慮此孝弟之大而推行之此所謂慮
之以大也孝弟莫先於愛愛而弗敬獸畜之也故設三老五更群老之席位
而敬無失焉此所謂愛之以敬也愛之而不以禮則失於徑情而直行故必親迎
肅入登歌合語而行之以禮焉徒禮之而不以養之則為無實而虛拘又必
適饌省醴作樂發咏而脩之以孝養焉孝養既脩又必下管象舞大武
以正君臣之位別貴賤之等而紀之以義焉然此篤近之禮而已又必命鄉
===
遂之群吏畿內之諸侯效法而舉行以及之於遠焉非終之以仁乎然始則
盡禮於一國終則推之於天下矣蓋養老之禮孝弟之道也人同此心心同此
道今也一舉於此則孝弟之道達於彼是以衆皆知其德之備者悉由于我
之所以一舉夫大事也謂非篤近而舉遠者其義為甚詳由此以達彼者其
德無不該乎抑又論之養老者孝弟之本而孝弟又治天下之本也虞夏
商周天下之盛王也未有遺年者非天子重養老之禮乎夫以萬乘之尊
而躬行其禮何哉豈非以親親長長必自吾身始而天下人人親其親長其長
而成大同之世歟故曰立愛惟親立敬惟長始于家邦終于四海豈虛語哉
古之聖人內之為尊外之為樂少之為貴多之為美是故先王
punctuated:
而達彼者，其德無不該。夫養老之禮，王道之大端也。今也聖人篤近以舉遠者，其義無不詳；則其推此而達彼者，其德又豈有不該者哉？記禮者知其然，謂夫虞、夏、商、周皆有養老之禮，後王亦皆記序前代之事也。然天子莫重於養老，人道莫大於孝弟。養老之禮，無非謀慮此孝弟之大而推行之，此所謂「慮之以大」也。孝弟莫先於愛，愛而弗敬，獸畜之也。故設三老、五更、群老之席位而敬無失焉，此所謂「愛之以敬」也。愛之而不以禮，則失於徑情而直行；故必親迎、肅入、登歌、合語，而「行之以禮」焉。徒禮之而不以養之，則為無實而虛拘；又必適饌、省醴、作樂、發咏，而「脩之以孝養」焉。孝養既脩，又必下管《象》、舞《大武》，以正君臣之位，別貴賤之等，而「紀之以義」焉。然此篤近之禮而已，又必命鄉遂之群吏、畿內之諸侯，效法而舉行，以及之於遠焉，非「終之以仁」乎？然始則盡禮於一國，終則推之於天下矣。蓋養老之禮，孝弟之道也。人同此心，心同此道。今也一舉於此，則孝弟之道達於彼；是以衆皆知其德之備者，悉由于我之所以一舉夫大事也。謂非篤近而舉遠者其義為甚詳，由此以達彼者其德無不該乎？抑又論之，養老者孝弟之本，而孝弟又治天下之本也。虞、夏、商、周，天下之盛王也，未有遺年者，非天子重養老之禮乎？夫以萬乘之尊而躬行其禮，何哉？豈非以親親長長必自吾身始，而天下人人親其親、長其長，而成大同之世歟？故曰：「立愛惟親，立敬惟長，始于家邦，終于四海。」豈虛語哉！
古之聖人，內之為尊，外之為樂；少之為貴，多之為美。是故先王
translation_en:
…to extend from here to there leaves no aspect of their virtue uncompassed. Now, the rite of nourishing the aged is a grand principle of the Kingly Way. When the sages devote themselves to what is near in order to raise up what is distant, the meaning is thoroughly detailed; and when they push from this to reach that, how could there be anything not encompassed by their virtue?

The recorder of the rites understood this to be so, stating that Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou all had the rite of nourishing the aged, and that later kings likewise recorded in order the affairs of preceding eras. Yet for the Son of Heaven, nothing is weightier than nourishing the aged, and in the way of humanity, nothing is greater than filial piety and fraternal respect. The rite of nourishing the aged is nothing other than deliberating upon the greatness of filial piety and fraternal respect and putting them into practice—this is what is meant by "deliberating upon it with greatness." In filial piety and fraternal respect, nothing comes before love; yet to love without respect is to keep them like beasts. Therefore, one sets the mats and places for the Three Elders (sanlao), the Five Experienced Men (wugeng), and the multitude of the aged so that respect is never lost—this is what is meant by "loving them with respect." To love them without ritual is to err by giving rein to raw emotion and acting without restraint; therefore, one must personally welcome them, usher them in with reverence, have the singers ascend, and engage in harmonious discourse, thus "conducting it with ritual." Merely to treat them with ritual without nourishing them would be empty detention devoid of substance; therefore, one must also go to the food offerings, inspect the sweet wine, strike up the music, and intone the songs, thus "cultivating it with filial nourishment." Once filial nourishment is cultivated, the pipes below must play the Xiang and the dancers perform the Dawu to rectify the positions of ruler and minister and distinguish the ranks of noble and base, thus "regulating it with righteousness." Yet all this is merely the rite of devoting oneself to what is near; one must further command the various officials of the districts and outlying areas, as well as the feudal lords within the royal domain, to emulate and perform it so that it reaches afar—is this not "consummating it with benevolence"? Thus, in the beginning one exhausts ritual within a single state, and in the end one extends it to the entire realm.

Indeed, the rite of nourishing the aged is the way of filial piety and fraternal respect. All people share this heart, and all hearts share this Way. Now, by performing this one act here, the way of filial piety and fraternal respect reaches there; therefore, the multitude all know that the completeness of his virtue stems entirely from his single performance of this great affair. Can we not say that in devoting oneself to what is near and raising up what is distant, the meaning is thoroughly detailed, and in extending from this to reach that, no aspect of virtue is left uncompassed?

To discuss this further: nourishing the aged is the root of filial piety and fraternal respect, and filial piety and fraternal respect are in turn the root of governing the realm. The rulers of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou were the flourishing kings of the world, and none of them neglected old age—was this not because the Son of Heaven attached great weight to the rite of nourishing the aged? Why would one of the exalted status of a lord of ten thousand chariots personally perform this rite? Is it not because treating one's kin as kin and one's elders as elders must begin with one's own person, so that everyone in the world will treat their kin as kin and their elders as elders, thereby bringing about an era of Great Harmony? Therefore it is said: "The establishment of love begins with kin; the establishment of respect begins with elders; it starts in the family and the state, and ends in completion throughout the four seas." Are these empty words?

The sages of antiquity took what is internal as venerable, and what is external as joyful; they took fewness as precious, and abundance as admirable. Therefore, when the former kings…

title: 宣德元年福建鄉試錄
text:
之制禮也不可多也不可寡也唯其稱也
同考試官訓導柴批〔四書三篇文理簡順禮經四篇皆熟於經文講習有素此篇發揮內外多寡之義粲〕
〔然可見如觀尺璧畧無纖玷場中礼經無出其右者論策俱有發越尤稱前場〕〔高薦何忝〕
考試官教諭邵批〔此篇經旨明白文辭簡淨必深於禮經者宜居前列〕
考試官前侍講余批〔初場七篇理明辭暢冠乎衆作此篇尤有發越場中所未及論策俱優誠有學之〕
〔士也寘之首選尤愜輿論〕
三名鄭亮
〔破得旨〕觀聖人之行禮隨所寓而有不同當觀聖人之制禮隨所施而無不當夫禮貴
===
乎稱而已然聖人之禮雖有內外多寡之不同又豈可過於中而不得其當哉且
夫古之聖人必有德有位之聖人也〔說得明白他卷言不及此〕其為禮者果何如耶盖致其敬而誠若者
心之寓於內者也心寓乎內則純誠之懿幽隱而難窮德產之致微妙而莫測
方寸之間惟精惟一豈不以內為尊乎有美而文而誠若者心之寓乎外者也
心寓乎外則發育萬物吾仁之形著大理物博吾德之發揚心與物交歡忻
悅懌豈不以外為樂乎心之所寓既有不同禮之所施豈無或異是故至
敬無文祭天特牲此禮之以少為貴也外盡其物儀文備舉此禮之以多為
美也其少者豈徒少哉一心之和足以備兩間之和一心之理足以該萬物之理
故不能不以少為貴焉其多者豈徒多哉三牲不備不足以盡祭祀之誠
punctuated:
之制禮也，不可多也，不可寡也，唯其稱也。
同考試官訓導柴批：〔四書三篇，文理簡順；禮經四篇，皆熟於經文，講習有素。此篇發揮內外多寡之義，粲〕〔然可見，如觀尺璧，畧無纖玷，場中礼經無出其右者。論策俱有發越，尤稱前場，〕〔高薦何忝。〕
考試官教諭邵批：〔此篇經旨明白，文辭簡淨，必深於禮經者，宜居前列。〕
考試官前侍講余批：〔初場七篇，理明辭暢，冠乎衆作。此篇尤有發越，場中所未及。論策俱優，誠有學之〕〔士也，寘之首選，尤愜輿論。〕
三名鄭亮
〔破得旨〕觀聖人之行禮，隨所寓而有不同；當觀聖人之制禮，隨所施而無不當。夫禮，貴乎稱而已。然聖人之禮，雖有內外多寡之不同，又豈可過於中而不得其當哉？且夫古之聖人，必有德有位之聖人也。〔說得明白，他卷言不及此〕其為禮者果何如耶？盖致其敬而誠若者，心之寓於內者也。心寓乎內，則純誠之懿，幽隱而難窮；德產之致，微妙而莫測。方寸之間，惟精惟一，豈不以內為尊乎？有美而文而誠若者，心之寓乎外者也。心寓乎外，則發育萬物，吾仁之形著；大理物博，吾德之發揚。心與物交，歡忻悅懌，豈不以外為樂乎？心之所寓既有不同，禮之所施豈無或異？是故至敬無文，祭天特牲，此禮之以少為貴也；外盡其物，儀文備舉，此禮之以多為美也。其少者，豈徒少哉？一心之和，足以備兩間之和；一心之理，足以該萬物之理，故不能不以少為貴焉。其多者，豈徒多哉？三牲不備，不足以盡祭祀之誠；
translation_en:
…instituted the rites, they could neither be too many nor too few, but simply matched what was fitting.”

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Chai: [His three essays on the Four Books are concise and smooth in reasoning and style; his four essays on the Classic of Rites all show familiarity with the scriptural text and well-practiced study. This essay elaborates the meaning of internal and external, many and few, with brilliant clarity—like beholding a foot-wide jade disk without the slightest flaw. Among the candidates taking the Classic of Rites in the examination hall, none surpasses him. His discourse and policy essays also show outstanding insight, well matching his performance in the first session. How could a high recommendation be undeserved?]

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Shao: [In this essay the meaning of the Classic is clear and the diction is concise and pure. He must be someone deeply versed in the Classic of Rites, and ought to be placed in the front ranks.]

Comment by Examiner and former Expositor-in-Waiting Yu: [In the seven essays of the first session, his reasoning is clear and his expression fluent, crowning all the other compositions. This essay shows particular insight that no other in the hall reached. His discourse and policy essays are both excellent; he is truly a scholar of learning. Placing him as the first choice especially satisfies public opinion.]

Third Place: Zheng Liang 鄭亮

[The opening captures the thesis.] When we observe how the sages practiced the rites, we see that they varied according to where the mind was lodged; we ought then to observe how the sages instituted the rites, seeing that they were never inappropriate in how they were applied. Now the rites value nothing other than suitability. Yet although the rites of the sages differed in being internal or external, many or few, how could they ever exceed the mean and fail to attain what is proper?

Moreover, the sages of antiquity were necessarily sages who possessed both virtue and position. [Explained clearly; other papers failed to mention this.] How, then, did they practice the rites? Truly, to carry reverence to the utmost so that sincerity is manifest is the mind lodged within. When the mind is lodged within, the excellence of pure sincerity is deep, hidden, and hard to exhaust; the subtlety of the workings of virtue is delicate and unfathomable. Within the square inch of the heart, being discerning and undivided—is this not taking the internal as exalted? To possess beauty and refinement so that sincerity is manifest is the mind lodged without. When the mind is lodged without, then in nourishing the myriad things, our benevolence takes manifest form; in the grand ordering of abundant things, our virtue is displayed. As the mind interacts with things in joy and delight—is this not taking the external as joyful?

Since where the mind is lodged differs, how could the application of the rites not also vary? Therefore, the utmost reverenceis without ornament, and in sacrificing to Heaven a single victim is used—this is the rites taking paucity as贵 (noble/precious). Externally exhausting all material offerings and fully performing every ceremonial form—this is the rites taking abundance as admirable. As for their being few, is it merely a matter of small numbers? The harmony of a single mind is sufficient to encompass the harmony of Heaven and Earth; the principle of a single mind is sufficient to embrace the principles of the myriad things—thus one cannot but value paucity in them. As for their being many, is it merely a matter of large numbers? If the three sacrificial beasts are not complete, it is insufficient to exhaust the sincerity of sacrifice; …

title: 宣德元年福建鄉試錄
text:
八簋不實不足以表吾心之敬故不能不以多為美焉然禮之行如此聖人
制禮豈可以異於此哉吾見古之先王任君師之責秉制禮之柄商度乎多
寡之宜詳審乎時中之道制其禮之少者如天子無介繁纓一就孰不以為
過乎儉也殊不知少者禮之隱隱非不足之謂而不可以增益也苟可以增益
則奢而過於禮安得謂之稱乎制其禮之多者如天子七廟二十有六豆孰不
以為過乎奢也殊不知多者禮之費費非有餘之謂而不可以減損也苟可
以減損則儉而不及於禮矣又安得謂之稱乎吁羔豚而祭百官皆足太牢
而祭不必有餘此之謂稱也聖人制禮豈有不稱哉大抵心者禮之存禮者心
之發天下之禮簡者非徒簡也必有為之簡者焉詳者非徒詳也必有為
===
之詳者焉記禮者於此既曰古之聖人又曰先王皆欲其禮之稱是拳拳然致謹
於後人者深矣學者豈可以不法先王之遺意哉然則管仲之山節藻梲
晏嬰之豚肩不掩豆是〔點尤妖〕皆謂之不知禮
punctuated: 八簋不實，不足以表吾心之敬，故不能不以多為美焉。然禮之行如此，聖人制禮，豈可以異於此哉？吾見古之先王，任君師之責，秉制禮之柄，商度乎多寡之宜，詳審乎時中之道。制其禮之少者，如天子無介、繁纓一就，孰不以為過乎儉也？殊不知少者禮之隱，隱非不足之謂，而不可以增益也；苟可以增益，則奢而過於禮，安得謂之稱乎？制其禮之多者，如天子七廟、二十有六豆，孰不以為過乎奢也？殊不知多者禮之費，費非有餘之謂，而不可以減損也；苟可以減損，則儉而不及於禮矣，又安得謂之稱乎？吁！羔豚而祭，百官皆足；太牢而祭，不必有餘，此之謂稱也。聖人制禮，豈有不稱哉？大抵心者禮之存，禮者心之發。天下之禮，簡者非徒簡也，必有為之簡者焉；詳者非徒詳也，必有為之詳者焉。記禮者於此，既曰「古之聖人」，又曰「先王」，皆欲其禮之稱，是拳拳然致謹於後人者深矣，學者豈可以不法先王之遺意哉？然則管仲之山節藻梲，晏嬰之豚肩不掩豆，是〔點尤妖〕皆謂之不知禮。
translation_en: … and if the eight *gui* vessels are not filled, it is insufficient to manifest the reverence of one's mind; therefore one cannot but take abundance as beauty. Yet since the practice of ritual is like this, when the sages established rituals, how could they differ from this? I see that the former kings of antiquity bore the responsibilities of ruler and teacher and held the authority to establish rituals, weighing the appropriateness of abundance and scarcity and carefully examining the Way of timely equilibrium. When they established rituals characterized by scarcity—such as the Son of Heaven having no attendant, or his horse's girth-tassel having only a single loop—who would not consider this overly frugal? They fail to realize that scarcity is the hiddenness (*yin*) of ritual; hiddenness does not mean insufficiency, and nothing can be added to it. If anything could be added to it, it would be extravagant and exceed ritual—how could it be called fitting? When they established rituals characterized by abundance—such as the Son of Heaven having seven ancestral temples, or twenty-six *dou* vessels—who would not consider this overly extravagant? They fail to realize that abundance is the广manifestation (*fei*) of ritual; manifestation does not mean surplus, and nothing can be subtracted from it. If anything could be subtracted from it, it would be frugal and fall short of ritual—how again could it be called fitting? Ah! "When sacrificing with a lamb and a suckling pig, all the officials are satisfied; when sacrificing with the Grand Victim (*tailao*), there is not necessarily any surplus: this is what is called being fitting." When the sages established rituals, how could there be anything unfitting? In general, the mind is where ritual is preserved, and ritual is the manifestation of the mind. Among the rituals in the world, those that are simple are not merely simple—there is necessarily a reason that makes them simple; those that are elaborate are not merely elaborate—there is necessarily a reason that makes them elaborate. In recording ritual here, the writer first says "the sages of antiquity" and then says "the former kings," in both cases desiring that their rituals be fitting. In this, his earnest care in admonishing posterity is profound indeed! How could scholars fail to model themselves on the bequeathed intentions of the former kings? Even so, Guan Zhong's mountain-carved capitals and duckweed-painted king-posts, and Yan Ying's suckling-pig shoulder not covering the *dou* vessel—these [comment: a particularly striking touch (點尤妙) [?]] are both called not knowing ritual.

title: 宣德元年福建鄉試錄
text:
授人時舜在璇璣玉衡以齊七政則制器尚象上有以推測乎天
道慎徽五典下有以明叙乎人倫皆所以繼天立極者也堯傳之舜
舜傳之禹則曰允執厥中是聖人繼天立極之道不外乎中也湯曰
建中建極武王曰皇建其有極是繼天之道亦不外乎中也中や極
也皆自上古聖神相繼而傳道統者也觀其叙曰天叙秩曰天秩
立父子之親定君臣之義於夫婦也教之以有别於長幼朋友也教
之以序以信所謂立人極者此也盖全體自然曰天聖人承其自然
故於天而謂之繼人物標準曰極聖人制其當然故於極而謂之
立天道也人極也皆具於聖人之心而敷教於天下後世者也故于朱
===
子序中庸之書而著其繼天立極之言以見聖人之相傳有自來
矣吁達而上古聖神二帝三王有以行繼天立極之道於當時窮而
在下有孔子顏曾思孟有以傳繼天立極之道於萬世堯舜遠
矣孔子邈矣洪惟
太祖高皇帝稟聖神文武之資備仁義禮智之德
太宗文皇帝道包六合德冠百王
仁宗昭皇帝行二帝三王之道體二帝三王之心是皆繼天立極以傳前聖
之統者也
皇上德侔天地明並日月繼志述事以承
punctuated: 授人時，舜在璇璣玉衡以齊七政，則制器尚象，上有以推測乎天道；慎徽五典，下有以明叙乎人倫，皆所以繼天立極者也。堯傳之舜，舜傳之禹，則曰：「允執厥中。」是聖人繼天立極之道，不外乎中也。湯曰：「建中建極。」武王曰：「皇建其有極。」是繼天之道，亦不外乎中也。中也、極也，皆自上古聖神相繼而傳道統者也。觀其叙曰「天叙」，秩曰「天秩」；立父子之親，定君臣之義；於夫婦也，教之以有别；於長幼、朋友也，教之以序、以信，所謂立人極者此也。盖全體自然曰天，聖人承其自然，故於天而謂之繼；人物標準曰極，聖人制其當然，故於極而謂之立。天道也、人極也，皆具於聖人之心，而敷教於天下後世者也。故于朱子序《中庸》之書，而著其「繼天立極」之言，以見聖人之相傳有自來矣。吁！達而上古聖神、二帝三王，有以行繼天立極之道於當時；窮而在下，有孔子、顏、曾、思、孟，有以傳繼天立極之道於萬世。堯、舜遠矣，孔子邈矣！洪惟太祖高皇帝稟聖神文武之資，備仁義禮智之德；太宗文皇帝道包六合，德冠百王；仁宗昭皇帝行二帝三王之道，體二帝三王之心，是皆繼天立極以傳前聖之統者也。皇上德侔天地，明並日月，繼志述事以承
translation_en: …to deliver the seasons to the people; and Shun examined the jade-adorned armillary sphere and sighting tube to bring into harmony the Seven Regulators—thus, by fashioning instruments and esteeming celestial images, above they had the means to fathom the Way of Heaven; and by carefullybeautifying the Five Canons, below they had the means to clearly order human relationships. All of these were the means by which they succeeded Heaven and established the ultimate standard. When Yao transmitted it to Shun, and Shun transmitted it to Yu, they said: "Sincerely hold fast the Mean." Thus the Way by which the sages succeeded Heaven and established the ultimate standard lies in nothing outside the Mean. Tang said: "Establish the Mean, establish the ultimate standard." King Wu said: "The August One establishes his ultimate standard." Thus the Way of succeeding Heaven also lies in nothing outside the Mean. Both the Mean and the ultimate standard are that by which the divine sages from high antiquity succeeded one another in transmitting the succession of the Way (daotong). Observe how its social arrangements are called "Heaven's arrangements," and its ritual order is called "Heaven's order." Establishing the affection between father and son, fixing the duty between ruler and minister, teaching distinction between husband and wife, and teaching precedence between old and young and trustworthiness between friends—this is what is meant by establishing the ultimate standard for humankind. For that which is completely spontaneous in its entirety is called Heaven; the sage inherits its spontaneity, and therefore with respect to Heaven it is called "succeeding." The standard for human beings and things is called the ultimate standard; the sage regulates what ought to be, and therefore with respect to the ultimate standard it is called "establishing." Both the Way of Heaven and the ultimate standard for humankind are complete within the mind of the sage, and are spread forth as teachings to all under Heaven and to future generations. Therefore, in Master Zhu's [Zhu Xi 朱熹] preface to the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), he set forth his words on "succeeding Heaven and establishing the ultimate standard" in order to show that the transmission from sage to sage had its origin. Alas! When in high station, the divine sages of high antiquity, the Two Emperors and Three Kings, had the means to practice the Way of succeeding Heaven and establishing the ultimate standard in their own times; when in obscurity and low station, Confucius, Yan [Yan Hui 顏回], Zeng [Zengzi 曾子], Si [Zisi 子思], and Meng [Mencius 孟子] had the means to transmit the Way of succeeding Heaven and establishing the ultimate standard to ten thousand generations. Yao and Shun are distant indeed; Confucius is far away indeed! Yet we reverently reflect that the Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu Gaohuangdi), was endowed with sagely, divine, civil, and martial qualities, and was complete in the virtues of humanity, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom; the Grand Ancestor, Emperor Wen (Taizong Wenhuangdi), encompassed the six directions with his Way and crowned the hundred kings with his virtue; and the Benevolent Ancestor, Emperor Zhao (Renzong Zhaohuangdi), practiced the Way of the Two Emperors and Three Kings and embodied the mind of the Two Emperors and Three Kings. All of them succeeded Heaven and established the ultimate standard so as to transmit the succession of the former sages. His Majesty the reigning Emperor matches Heaven and Earth in virtue, equals the sun and moon in brilliance, and carries forward their intentions and continues their enterprises so as to inherit…

title: 宣德元年福建鄉試錄
text:
三聖之統故曰先聖後聖其揆一也敢以是為論
擬唐虞世南上聖德論表十九名龔錡
考試官教諭邵批表得唐體語不雷同
考試官前侍講余批典雅可觀
切以
天開景運膺曆數之在躬世際雍熈握乾符而受命一人有慶四海
咸歸六合同春兆民是賴恭惟
〇〇〇〇天錫勇智大興湯武之師日新聖明上繼唐虞之治功高莫極
德盛難名得惟精惟一之傳紹乃武乃文之聖求賢常若不及
===
從諫有如轉丸惟五帝足以比其休匪三王莫能方其盛山高
海闊曷伸賛頌之辭日照月臨奚罄名言之妙臣一介賤士三
才末流叨蒙館職之榮素乏論思之益丹衷激切敢効言於芻
蕘
睿覽昭明庶鑒誠於葵藿尚冀緝熈聖學川方至而日方升鞏固
皇圖天與長而地與久謹撰聖德論隨表上進
第三塲
策
第一問一名林時望
punctuated:
三聖之統，故曰「先聖後聖，其揆一也」。敢以是為論。

擬唐虞世南上《聖德論》表。十九名龔錡。
考試官教諭邵批：表得唐體，語不雷同。
考試官前侍講余批：典雅可觀。

切以天開景運，膺曆數之在躬；世際雍熈，握乾符而受命。一人有慶，四海咸歸；六合同春，兆民是賴。恭惟〇〇〇〇天錫勇智，大興湯、武之師；日新聖明，上繼唐、虞之治。功高莫極，德盛難名。得惟精惟一之傳，紹乃武乃文之聖。求賢常若不及，從諫有如轉丸。惟五帝足以比其休，匪三王莫能方其盛。山高海闊，曷伸賛頌之辭；日照月臨，奚罄名言之妙。臣一介賤士，三才末流。叨蒙館職之榮，素乏論思之益。丹衷激切，敢効言於芻蕘；睿覽昭明，庶鑒誠於葵藿。尚冀緝熈聖學，川方至而日方升；鞏固皇圖，天與長而地與久。謹撰《聖德論》隨表上進。

第三塲。
策。
第一問，一名林時望。
translation_en:
… the succession of the Three Sages. Therefore it is said: "Former sages and later sages—their principles are one and the same." I venture to present this as my discourse.

Imitating the Tang-dynasty official Yu Shinan's 虞世南 "Memorial Presenting the Discourse on Sagely Virtue" (Shang Shengde lun biao 上聖德論表). Ranked 19th: Gong Qi 龔錡.
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Shao commented: The memorial captures the Tang style, and its phrasing is free of clichés.
Examiner and former Expositor-in-Waiting Yu commented: Classically elegant and worthy of admiration.

I humbly reflect that as Heaven opens a glorious cycle, Your Majesty bears the calendar of succession in your own person; as the world encounters an era of harmonious peace, you grasp the talisman of Heaven and receive the Mandate. When the One Man rejoices, all within the Four Seas submit; as the Six Directions share in the spring, the millions of common people rely upon you. I reverently reflect that [Your Majesty, the Emperor], endowed by Heaven with courage and wisdom, raised a great army like those of Tang 湯 and Wu 武; daily renewing your sagely intelligence, you look upward to continue the governance of Tang 唐 [Yao 堯] and Yu 虞 [Shun 舜]. Your achievements are so lofty as to be boundless, and your virtue is so flourishing as to be beyond description. You have obtained the transmission of "beingrefined and single-minded," and have carried on the sageliness of being "both martial and civil." You seek worthy men as though always fearing to fall short, and follow remonstrance as smoothly as rolling a pellet. Only the Five Emperors suffice to be compared to your splendor; none but the Three Kings can match your flourishing grandeur. As high as the mountains and as wide as the seas, how could one fully express words of praise and eulogy? As the sun shines and the moon looks down, how could one exhaust the subtlety of descriptive language? Your servant is a lowly scholar of mean station, at the very bottom of the triad of Heaven, Earth, and Man. Having unworthily received the honor of an academic post, I have long lacked any contribution of counsel and reflection. Yet my loyal heart is deeply stirred, so I dare to offer words like a humble grass-cutter and firewood-gatherer; before your sagely and bright perusal, I hope you may recognize a sincerity like the sunflower turning toward the sun. Still more do I hope that you will continue to render radiant your sagely learning, like a river swelling at the flood and the sun just rising; and that you will consolidate the imperial domain, enduring as long as Heaven and Earth. I have reverently composed the "Discourse on Sagely Virtue" (Shengde lun 聖德論) and present it herewith accompanying this memorial.

Third Session.
Policy Essays.
First Question, ranked 1st: Lin Shiwang 林時望.

title: 宣德元年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官進士方批〔文勢滔滔不冗不泛兼以四君子自期誠抱負卓然之士矣〕
考試官教諭邵批〔此策不拘拘於問目以胸中素蘊吐辭成文學識優長抱負不小他日所就其可量乎深加敬羡〕
考試官前侍講余批〔辭意高邁志氣超卓出群拔萃者也〕
高崗之鳳必於隆盛之世而始鳴大野之麟必於文明之時而始見
負有為之人才必於聖明之君而後出焉此氣類之相感理勢之必然
夫豈偶然之故哉棘闈秋開多士雲集執事典文衡策承學首
以
大誥陰隲書為問豈以當代之制作正學者所當講也請因明問以復可乎夫
有一代之君必有一代之臣有一代之臣必匡一代之治恭惟
===
太祖高皇帝稟聰明睿智之資備聖神文武之德龍飛江左統馭華夷拳
拳以福民為心切切以圖治為務萬機之暇條成
大誥於序有曰立綱陳紀為民造福又曰君臣同心志同一氣大哉
皇言乎其望群臣同心輔弼共成一代之治乎故自蒞祚以來餘六十年其間
或以碩才而居廟堂或以正直而司風紀職方面者濟濟乎有為之
賢任守令者彬彬乎有能之士內外之臣不同而立綱陳紀者同一心大
小之職不一而為民造福者同一志故能措天下於泰山躋黎元於仁壽
材生總聚者咸席景星慶雲之下聚廬托處者同囿春臺玉燭之中
其治效之隆殆與唐虞黎民於變之風三代直道而行之俗同一轍矣
punctuated:
同考試官進士方批〔文勢滔滔，不冗不泛，兼以四君子自期，誠抱負卓然之士矣。〕
考試官教諭邵批〔此策不拘拘於問目，以胸中素蘊吐辭成文，學識優長，抱負不小，他日所就其可量乎？深加敬羡。〕
考試官前侍講余批〔辭意高邁，志氣超卓，出群拔萃者也。〕
高崗之鳳，必於隆盛之世而始鳴；大野之麟，必於文明之時而始見；負有為之人才，必於聖明之君而後出焉。此氣類之相感，理勢之必然，夫豈偶然之故哉？棘闈秋開，多士雲集，執事典文衡，策承學，首以《大誥》、《陰隲》書為問，豈以當代之制作，正學者所當講也？請因明問以復，可乎？夫有一代之君，必有一代之臣；有一代之臣，必匡一代之治。恭惟太祖高皇帝稟聰明睿智之資，備聖神文武之德，龍飛江左，統馭華夷，拳拳以福民為心，切切以圖治為務。萬機之暇，條成《大誥》，於序有曰：「立綱陳紀，為民造福。」又曰：「君臣同心，志同一氣。」大哉皇言乎！其望群臣同心輔弼，共成一代之治乎！故自蒞祚以來餘六十年，其間或以碩才而居廟堂，或以正直而司風紀，職方面者濟濟乎有為之賢，任守令者彬彬乎有能之士。內外之臣不同，而立綱陳紀者同一心；大小之職不一，而為民造福者同一志。故能措天下於泰山，躋黎元於仁壽，材生總聚者咸席景星慶雲之下，聚廬托處者同囿春臺玉燭之中。其治效之隆，殆與唐、虞黎民於變之風，三代直道而行之俗，同一轍矣。
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner and Metropolitan Graduate (jinshi) Fang: [The momentum of the prose flows on in a mighty torrent, neither wordy nor unfocused; moreover, by taking the four noble men as his personal model, he is truly a scholar of outstanding aspirations.]
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Shao: [This policy essay does not bind itself slavishly to the items of the question, but pours forth words into prose from the store long cherished in his breast. His learning and insight are superior, and his aspirations are by no means small—how could his future achievements be measured? I deeply admire and esteem it.]
Comment by Examiner and former Expositor-in-waiting Yu: [Its words and ideas are lofty and far-reaching, its ambition and spirit transcendent—truly one who stands out above the crowd.]
The phoenix on the high ridge sings only in an age of flourishing prosperity; the unicorn in the great wilderness appears only in a time of radiant culture; and men of talent who possess the capacity for great deeds emerge only when there is a sage and enlightened ruler. This is the mutual resonance of things of like vital force, the inevitable trend of principle and circumstance—how could it be a matter of mere chance? In autumn the thorny examination compound opens and the multitude of scholars gather like clouds. You, sir, preside over the literary balance and put policy questions to us junior scholars, asking first about the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao) and the book on Secret Merits (Yinzhi)—is this not because the institutions and compositions of the reigning dynasty are precisely what scholars ought to study and discuss? May I request permission to reply by following your perceptive question?
Now, where there is the ruler of an era, there must be the ministers of that era; and where there are the ministers of an era, they must assist in bringing about the governance of that era. I reverently reflect that Grand Progenitor Emperor Gao (Taizu Gao Huangdi) was endowed with sagacious and penetrating gifts and possessed complete sagehood, divinity, civil, and martial virtue. As a dragon he took flight East of the Yangtze, extending his rule over Chinese and barbarian alike, earnestly taking the blessing of the people as his heart's concern and urgently making the pursuit of good governance his task. In his leisure from the myriad affairs of state, he compiled the articles of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao), in the preface of which it is said: "To establish the overarching principles and set forth the regulations, creating blessings for the people." And again it is said: "Ruler and minister of one mind, their aspirations united in a single vital spirit." Great indeed are the Imperial words! How he hoped that all his ministers would assist him with one mind, jointly accomplishing the governance of the era!
Thus, in the more than sixty years since the dynasty ascended the throne, during that time some have occupied the imperial court by virtue of great talent, while others have presided over discipline and the风纪 [censorial oversight] through uprightness; those charged with regional administration have been an abundant host of accomplished worthies, and those appointed as prefects and magistrates have been a refined array of capable gentlemen. Though the officials of the inner court and outer provinces differ, they are of one mind in establishing the overarching principles and setting forth the regulations; though their offices great and small are not uniform, they share a single aspiration to create blessings for the people. Therefore they have been able to place the realm upon the security of Mount Tai and raise the common people to a state of benevolence and longevity; those of talent and vitality who gather together all sit beneath auspicious stars and felicitous clouds, while those who cluster their huts and make their dwellings are all encompassed within the spring terrace and the jade candle of harmonious seasons. The flourishing efficacy of this governance truly follows the very same track as the transforming customs of the black-haired people under Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun], and the mores of walking the straight path in the Three Dynasties.

title: 宣德元年福建鄉試錄
text:
太宗文皇帝纘承丕緒一遵
成憲道已至矣而尤以為未至治已隆矣而尤以為未隆心
太祖之心法
太祖之法庶務之餘采輯古今為善陰隲者百六十五人纂次成書梓行天
下其間若仲淹之經濟安撫江淮則民懷賑恤元昊犯順則請自
行邊趙抃之讞疑節度武安而辨赦後之冤出知成都而省劔
民之死富弼守青州而活京東之流民蘇軾知徐州而禦彭城之
水患之數君子者無非政績之顯於當時者也然
太祖大誥之頒豈徒然歟蓋欲群臣佩服
===
聖誥之旨而以福民為心也
太宗陰隲之布豈無意歟蓋欲天下遍觀前代之賢以為今日之法也愚
也欽承三誥一書已久樂菁莪之教已深其於明體適用之
學雖未可知與斯賓興之典行將嚮用使他日居廟堂之
高必以仲淹之心為心司風紀之要必以趙抃之法為法方面
之職必欲踵跡於富弼守令之任必欲比肩於蘇軾豈使數
君子專美於前代乎恭承明問姑述其槩以復願進教之
幸甚
punctuated:
太宗文皇帝纘承丕緒，一遵成憲，道已至矣，而尤以為未至；治已隆矣，而尤以為未隆。心太祖之心，法太祖之法，庶務之餘，采輯古今《為善陰隲》者百六十五人，纂次成書，梓行天下。其間若仲淹之經濟，安撫江淮則民懷賑恤，元昊犯順則請自行邊；趙抃之讞疑，節度武安而辨赦後之冤，出知成都而省劔民之死；富弼守青州而活京東之流民；蘇軾知徐州而禦彭城之水患。之數君子者，無非政績之顯於當時者也。然太祖《大誥》之頒，豈徒然歟？蓋欲群臣佩服聖誥之旨，而以福民為心也。太宗《陰隲》之布，豈無意歟？蓋欲天下遍觀前代之賢，以為今日之法也。

愚也欽承三《誥》、一書已久，樂菁莪之教已深。其於明體適用之學，雖未可知，與斯賓興之典，行將嚮用。使他日居廟堂之高，必以仲淹之心為心；司風紀之要，必以趙抃之法為法；方面之職，必欲踵跡於富弼；守令之任，必欲比肩於蘇軾。豈使數君子專美於前代乎？恭承明問，姑述其槩以復，願進教之，幸甚。
translation_en:
When Emperor Wen, Taizong (the Yongle Emperor), succeeded to the great enterprise, he wholly followed the established constitutions. The Way had already reached its pinnacle, yet he still considered it unattained; governance was already flourishing, yet he still considered it insufficiently exalted. Taking the heart of Taizu (the Hongwu Emperor) as his own heart, and modeling himself on the laws of Taizu, in his leisure from state affairs he gathered records of one hundred and sixty-five individuals from antiquity to the present for the Hidden Rewards for Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi), compiled them into a book, and had it printed and circulated throughout the realm. Among them were figures such as Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹 with his statecraft: when serving as Pacification Commissioner of the Jiang-Huai region, the people cherished his famine relief, and when Yuanhao rebelled against imperial authority, he requested to go in person to inspect the frontier; Zhao Bian 趙抃 with his resolution of doubtful legal cases: while serving in the Wu'an Military Command, he cleared an injustice committed after an amnesty, and when sent out as Prefect of Chengdu, he spared the lives of the people of Jianzhou; Fu Bi 富弼, who as Prefect of Qingzhou saved the refugees of Jingdong; and Su Shi 蘇軾, who as Prefect of Xuzhou warded off the flood disasters at Pengcheng. All of these several noble men were none other than those whose administrative achievements were illustrious in their own times. Yet was Taizu's promulgation of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao) in vain? Surely he desired that all his officials take to heart the purport of the sagely pronouncements and make blessing the people their core intention. And was Taizong's dissemination of the Hidden Rewards (Yinzhi) without purpose? Surely he desired that the whole world broadly observe the worthies of former dynasties and take them as models for today.

Ignorant as I am, I have reverently received the three Grand Pronouncements and the one book [Hidden Rewards for Doing Good] for a long time, and have deeply rejoiced in the nurturing education of the schools. As for the learning that illuminates fundamental principles and applies them to practical use, although I cannot claim to know it fully, having participated in this ceremony of recommending worthies for the examination, I am about to be employed in office. Should I one day occupy a high position at court, I shall certainly take the heart of Fan Zhongyan as my heart; should I be in charge of the vital posts of moral discipline and censorship, I shall certainly take the methods of Zhao Bian as my model; in a regional or provincial post, I shall certainly wish to follow in the footsteps of Fu Bi; and in the office of prefect or magistrate, I shall certainly wish to stand shoulder to shoulder with Su Shi. How could we allow those few noble men to monopolize such distinction in former dynasties? Reverently receiving your enlightened question, I provisionally set forth this general outline in reply, and earnestly hope you will offer further instruction—how fortunate that would be!

title: 宣德元年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試小錄序
聖天子纘承
三聖大一統之業率由舊章誕敷文教方側席求賢以弘熙洽之治廼
省宣德紀元之初
命天下方岳重臣奉行賓興之禮於是福建藩臬諸公先期聘
戒群儒以司文柄啓院之日八郡之士抱其藝而入試者
五百餘人內則有監察御史豫章王公璉會稽范公宗淵
姚陽王公寶清江張公鐸憲使金華邵公玘左參政永嘉
楊公景衡憲副金華祝公戒僉憲衛輝王公生以董其
===
事外則參政姑蘇彭公森憲副淮陰成公寧可參議南
陽樊公翰僉憲匡南陶公瑋以維持之御史王范二公
告戒於諸執事曰今欽定解額所以去利誘也務得實
材以資
國用自是陳列者莫不協恭於廼職將撤棘取合格之士四
十五人遵
定制也小錄既成諸公謂予不可無序以弁其端洪惟
國朝自開創以來統一寰海垂六十年矣混合三光五嶽之
氣熏涵融液於兩間以致四方之賢士彙出人物益隆
punctuated:
福建鄉試小錄序

聖天子纘承三聖大一統之業，率由舊章，誕敷文教，方側席求賢，以弘熙洽之治。廼者宣德紀元之初，命天下方岳重臣奉行賓興之禮。於是福建藩臬諸公，先期聘戒群儒，以司文柄。啓院之日，八郡之士抱其藝而入試者五百餘人。內則有監察御史豫章王公璉、會稽范公宗淵、姚陽王公寶、清江張公鐸，憲使金華邵公玘，左參政永嘉楊公景衡，憲副金華祝公戒，僉憲衛輝王公生，以董其事；外則參政姑蘇彭公森，憲副淮陰成公寧可，參議南陽樊公翰，僉憲匡南陶公瑋，以維持之。御史王、范二公，告戒於諸執事曰：「今欽定解額，所以去利誘也，務得實材，以資國用。」自是陳列者莫不協恭於廼職。將撤棘，取合格之士四十五人，遵定制也。小錄既成，諸公謂予不可無序以弁其端。

洪惟國朝自開創以來，統一寰海，垂六十年矣。混合三光五嶽之氣，熏涵融液於兩間，以致四方之賢士彙出，人物益隆，
translation_en:
Preface to the Concise Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

The sacred Son of Heaven has succeeded to the great unified enterprise of the Three Sacred Emperors. Following established statutes and widely spreading civil teachings, he now waits eagerly on the edge of his mat to seek out the worthy, so as to broaden his illustrious and harmonious rule. At the beginning of the Xuande reign period (1426), he commanded the senior provincial officials across the empire to carry out the rite of recommending worthy men as guests of the state. Thereupon, the gentlemen of the Fujian Provincial Administration Commission and Surveillance Commission invited and admonished a group of Confucian scholars ahead of time to take charge of the literary evaluations. On the day the examination compound opened, more than five hundred scholars from the eight prefectures brought their skills and entered to take the examination. Inside the compound, there were Investigating Censors Wang Lian 王璉 of Yuzhang, Fan Zongyuan 范宗淵 of Guiji, Wang Bao 王寶 of Yaoyang, and Zhang Duo 張鐸 of Qingjiang; Surveillance Commissioner Shao Qi 邵玘 of Jinhua; Left Administration Vice Commissioner Yang Jingheng 楊景衡 of Yongjia; Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhu Jie 祝戒 of Jinhua; and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Wang Sheng 王生 of Weihui, to direct its affairs. Outside, there were Administration Vice Commissioner Peng Sen 彭森 of Gusu, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Cheng Ningke 成寧可 of Huaiyin, Administration Assistant Commissioner Fan Han 樊翰 of Nanyang, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Tao Wei 陶瑋 of Kuangnan, to maintain order. The two Censors, Messrs. Wang and Fan, admonished the various functionaries, saying: "The imperial fixing of the provincial graduate quota today is meant to eliminate the lure of self-interest; we must strive to obtain men of genuine talent to aid the needs of the state." From that point on, all those arrayed at their posts worked in respectful harmony in their duties. As the thorny barriers of the compound were about to be removed, forty-five qualified scholars were selected, in compliance with the established quota. Once the concise record was completed, the gentlemen said that I could not decline to write a preface to place at its head.

Reflecting upon the grand history of our dynasty since its founding, it has unified the lands within the four seas for nearly sixty years. It has blended the vital energies of the sun, moon, stars, and Five Marchmounts, steeping and fusing them between Heaven and Earth, so that worthy scholars from all directions have emerged in great numbers, and men of talent have flourished ever more…

title: 宣德元年福建鄉試錄
text:
盖承平之久而上沐
煦育甄陶之化有以致之也稽之往古自孟子之後斯道
寢微歷漢暨唐雖有崇文之君校讐於石渠莫探其旨趣
討論於弘文從事乎葩藻千數百載之間而斯道莫之
振也迨乎炎宋濂洛關閩諸儒繼出有以上泝洙泗之源
而斯道復明自時而後註論群經者又不能無異同我
太祖高皇帝於功成治定之日乃召諸儒纂成書傳會選
太祖文皇帝於繼志述事之秋乃命諸儒臣輯成五經四書性理
大全盖折衷諸家之說而去取之皆頒其書於天下
===
仁宗昭皇帝闡明厥旨宣播之於萬方皆以是繼前聖之緒以嘉
惠來學以開千萬世文明之運猗歟盛哉竊惟往代群
經之義未合于一紛々論說派别岐分學者莫知適從
今之士子際乎
昭代述作之備不啻皎日中見夫坦々之周行無它岐之惑
由兹而進學方之往昔之人功必倍之宜乎四海文學之
懿頓超於前時也今觀所試之文如美玉之出山阜卿
雲之布太空煜々乎含光麗彩誠足以瑞世然此已見其
能明斯道之蘊則必欲行斯道於當時則必遵乎周行
punctuated: 盖承平之久，而上沐煦育甄陶之化，有以致之也。稽之往古，自孟子之後，斯道寢微。歷漢暨唐，雖有崇文之君，校讐於石渠，莫探其旨趣；討論於弘文，從事乎葩藻。千數百載之間，而斯道莫之振也。迨乎炎宋，濂、洛、關、閩諸儒繼出，有以上泝洙、泗之源，而斯道復明。自時而後，註論群經者又不能無異同。我太祖高皇帝於功成治定之日，乃召諸儒纂成《書傳會選》；太祖文皇帝於繼志述事之秋，乃命諸儒臣輯成《五經》、《四書》、《性理大全》，盖折衷諸家之說而去取之，皆頒其書於天下。仁宗昭皇帝闡明厥旨，宣播之於萬方。皆以是繼前聖之緒，以嘉惠來學，以開千萬世文明之運。猗歟盛哉！竊惟往代群經之義未合于一，紛々論說，派别岐分，學者莫知適從。今之士子，際乎昭代述作之備，不啻皎日中見夫坦々之周行，無它岐之惑。由兹而進學，方之往昔之人，功必倍之，宜乎四海文學之懿頓超於前時也。今觀所試之文，如美玉之出山阜，卿雲之布太空，煜々乎含光麗彩，誠足以瑞世。然此已見其能明斯道之蘊，則必欲行斯道於當時，則必遵乎周行，
translation_en:
… Surely this has been brought about by a long period of peace, during which they have been bathed from above in the transforming influence of nurturing warmth and careful molding. Examining antiquity, after Mencius this Way gradually declined. Through the Han and down to the Tang, although there were rulers who esteemed letters, those who collated texts in the Stone Canal Pavilion failed to plumb its essential meaning, and those who debated in the Institute for the Advancement of Literature busied themselves with flowery rhetoric. For well over a thousand years, this Way could not be revived. Coming down to the Song dynasty, the scholars of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min emerged in succession, able to trace back upstream to the source of the Zhu and Si rivers, and so this Way became clear once more. From that time onward, however, those who annotated and discussed the various Classics again could not avoid discrepancies and disagreements. On the day when his achievements were complete and governance was settled, our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu), summoned the Confucian scholars to compile the Selected Commentaries on the Book of Documents (Shuzhuan huixuan). At the time of carrying forward his predecessor's aims and continuing his undertakings, the Grand Ancestor [sic, for Taizong], Emperor Wen, commanded the Confucian officials to compile the Great Compendia on the Five Classics, Four Books, and Nature and Principle (Wujing Sishu Xingli daquan), weighing and harmonizing the explanations of the various schools to select and reject among them, and promulgated all these books throughout the realm. Emperor Zhao (Renzong) elucidated their purport and broadcast it to all regions. All of them thereby continued the heritage of the former sages, graciously benefiting future scholars and opening up an era of cultural brilliance for ten thousand generations. Oh, how magnificent!

I humbly reflect that in bygone dynasties the meanings of the various Classics were not unified; amid a welter of theories and arguments, schools split and paths diverged, so that scholars did not know which way to follow. Scholars of today, encountering the completeness of our illustrious era's compilations, are nothing less than people seeing a broad, level highway under the bright midday sun, without the confusion of branching paths. Advancing in learning from this foundation, compared with people of the past their achievements must be redoubled; it is fitting indeed that the excellence of literary learning within the four seas suddenly surpasses that of former times! Now, looking at the essays from this examination, they are like fine jade emerging from the hills or auspicious clouds spreading across the vast sky—brilliantly holding inner light and resplendent color, truly sufficient to serve as auspicious omens for the age. Yet since this already shows that they are able to understand the profundities of this Way, if they surely wish to practice this Way in the present day, they must follow the broad highway…

title: 宣德元年福建鄉試錄
text:
而發軔自兹始矣行見羽儀
天朝翊贊
盛治宣忠勵節以皐夔周召之勛業自期揚偉烈而垂之
竹帛則庶幾上副
三聖倡明正學垂訓後世之心亦不負
聖天子設科求賢之意矣是為序
宣德元年八月吉日前翰林侍講余鼎序
punctuated:
而發軔自兹始矣。行見羽儀天朝，翊贊盛治，宣忠勵節，以皐、夔、周、召之勛業自期，揚偉烈而垂之竹帛，則庶幾上副三聖倡明正學、垂訓後世之心，亦不負聖天子設科求賢之意矣。是為序。
宣德元年八月吉日，前翰林侍講余鼎序。
translation_en:
…and set their wheels in motion starting from this very point. Before long, we shall see them serve as plumed ornaments at the Celestial Court, assisting in the flourishing governance, displaying loyalty and sharpening their integrity, aspiring to the meritorious achievements of Gao Yao, Kui, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao, exalting great deeds and handing them down on bamboo and silk. In so doing, they may perhaps live up to the hearts of the Three Sages [Emperors Taizu, Taizong, and Renzong] in championing and illuminating orthodox learning to leave instructions for posterity, and also not disappoint the Sage Son of Heaven’s intention in establishing the examination system to seek out the worthy. This serves as the preface.
On an auspicious day in the eighth month of the first year of the Xuande reign [1426], prefaced by Yu Ding 余鼎, former Expositor-in-Waiting in the Hanlin Academy.

title: 宣德元年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉闈小錄序
自古有天下國家者一是皆以賢才爲本君子所以得
成其器行其道于時者必由學校科目所致也三代
養士用賢之効考於經可見歷漢唐宋之君既皆孳
孳學術故致治之盛幾於三代洪惟
國朝自
太祖高皇帝龍飛江左定鼎金陵聿新
昭代之儒風大舉斯文之墜典自
京師首善之地以至偏州下邑莫不建學立師甄陶士類
===
化洽風俗爰倣古制以設科取士黜詞賦以抑浮華去疑
問以除穿鑿本之五經四書以觀其蘊博之詔誥論判以
觀其識策之經史時務以繹其才由是賢哲奮庸布列
中外化行俗美政善民安是皆養賢用賢之効也継以
太宗文皇帝之紹述
仁宗昭皇帝之守成致治之盛餘六十年宜其賢才治効濟〻
乎颯〻乎無間於三代矣易曰聖人久於其道而天下化
成此之謂也
皇上以聖繼聖崇儒重道鐫解額以去利誘精選舉以表真才
punctuated:
福建鄉闈小錄序
自古有天下國家者，一是皆以賢才爲本。君子所以得成其器、行其道于時者，必由學校科目所致也。三代養士用賢之効，考於經可見。歷漢、唐、宋之君，既皆孳孳學術，故致治之盛，幾於三代。洪惟國朝，自太祖高皇帝龍飛江左，定鼎金陵，聿新昭代之儒風，大舉斯文之墜典。自京師首善之地，以至偏州下邑，莫不建學立師，甄陶士類，化洽風俗。爰倣古制以設科取士，黜詞賦以抑浮華，去疑問以除穿鑿；本之《五經》、《四書》以觀其蘊，博之詔、誥、論、判以觀其識，策之經史、時務以繹其才。由是賢哲奮庸，布列中外，化行俗美，政善民安，是皆養賢用賢之効也。継以太宗文皇帝之紹述，仁宗昭皇帝之守成，致治之盛餘六十年，宜其賢才治効濟〻乎、颯〻乎無間於三代矣。《易》曰：「聖人久於其道，而天下化成。」此之謂也。皇上以聖繼聖，崇儒重道，鐫解額以去利誘，精選舉以表真才。
translation_en:
Preface to the Short Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

Since antiquity, all who have possessed the empire and the state have without exception taken worthy talent as their foundation. The means by which gentlemen are able to perfect their capacities and put their Way into practice in their own time must come about through schools and examination categories. The efficacy of nurturing scholars and employing the worthy in the Three Dynasties can be seen when examined in the Classics. Through the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, the rulers were all assiduous in promoting scholarship, and thus the flourishing of their governance nearly approached that of the Three Dynasties.

Reflecting upon our august Dynasty: since Grand Progenitor Emperor Gao (Taizu, the Hongwu Emperor) soared like a dragon from Jiangzuo and established the imperial tripod at Jinling (Nanjing), he renewed the Confucian ethos of our illustrious age and grandly revived the fallen canons of this culture. From the Capital, the place of foremost excellence, down to remote prefectures and lowly districts, there was nowhere that did not establish schools and appoint teachers to mold the scholarly class and spread transformative influence throughout local customs. Thereupon, imitating ancient institutions, he established examination categories to select scholars: dismissing poetic expositions and rhapsodies to curb showy superficiality, and eliminating "questions and doubts" (yiwen) to eradicate forced interpretations; grounding them in the Five Classics and Four Books to observe their inner depth, broadening them with edicts,announcements, discourses, and legal judgments to observe their insight, and testing them with policy questions on the Classics, Histories, and current affairs to draw out their talent. From this, the worthy and wise rose to service and were arrayed throughout the court and the provinces; moral transformation proceeded and customs became fine, governance was good and the people were at peace—all of this was the effect of nurturing and employing the worthy.

Continued by Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen's (Taizong, the Yongle Emperor) carrying forward of the enterprise, and Benevolent Ancestor Emperor Zhao's (Renzong, the Hongxi Emperor) preservation of the accomplishments, the flourishing of good governance has lasted for more than sixty years. Fitting it is that the abundance of worthy talents and the efficacy of governance are so stately and magnificent, with no gap separating them from the Three Dynasties! The Book of Changes (Yi) says: "The sage perseveres long in his Way, and all under Heaven is transformed and brought to completion." This is what it means.

His Majesty the reigning Emperor, as a sage succeeding sages, reveres Confucianism and honors the Way, reducing the provincial quotas to remove the lure of profit and refining the selection process to manifest true talent. …

title: 宣德元年福建鄉試錄
text:
廼宣德紀元之秋属當大比福建藩臬祗奉
德意延聘文衡合八郡之士而試之于時臨蒞之嚴則有若
栢臺諸賢奉行之勤則有若藩臬諸公皆出自科目
心體正大防範嚴明暨內外執事之人罔不恪勤乃事公
論攸歸視歷科而不能及噫盛矣哉撤棘之日得士凡
四十五人小錄既成前翰林侍
講余先生序之詳矣復命為後序余聞士之有志于行道
者不以科目得失為輕重而以民之休戚為己憂先正有
言文章足以潤身政事可以澤物斯言也豈不信哉
===
聖天子嗣位之初而科目選舉之精一至于此誠欲得天下真才而
用之使之澤被生民流芳來裔夫豈區區求備於一時者
哉諸君子窮經待用得與茲選何其幸歟尚當取法
於古人以明體適用之學效用于時俾天下之民霑被其
澤後世稱為文章政事必科目之士也豈不偉歟尚勗
之
宣德元年秋八月下澣會稽邵思廡序
punctuated:
廼宣德紀元之秋，属當大比，福建藩臬祗奉德意，延聘文衡，合八郡之士而試之。于時臨蒞之嚴，則有若栢臺諸賢；奉行之勤，則有若藩臬諸公，皆出自科目，心體正大，防範嚴明；暨內外執事之人，罔不恪勤乃事。公論攸歸，視歷科而不能及。噫，盛矣哉！撤棘之日，得士凡四十五人。小錄既成，前翰林侍講余先生序之詳矣，復命為後序。余聞士之有志于行道者，不以科目得失為輕重，而以民之休戚為己憂。先正有言：「文章足以潤身，政事可以澤物。」斯言也，豈不信哉！聖天子嗣位之初，而科目選舉之精一至于此，誠欲得天下真才而用之，使之澤被生民，流芳來裔，夫豈區區求備於一時者哉？諸君子窮經待用，得與茲選，何其幸歟！尚當取法於古人，以明體適用之學效用于時，俾天下之民霑被其澤，後世稱為文章政事必科目之士也，豈不偉歟？尚勗之！
宣德元年秋八月下澣，會稽邵思廡序。
translation_en:
Now, in the autumn of the first year of the Xuande era (1426), it is the time of the triennial examination. The Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions of Fujian respectfully obeyed the imperial benevolent intent, invited the literary arbiters [Examiners], and gathered the scholars of the eight prefectures to test them. At this time, for sternness in supervision, there were the worthy censors of the Censorate; for diligence in execution, there were the gentlemen of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions. All of them rose through the examination system; their minds and substance are upright and grand, and their precautions and regulations are strict and clear. Along with the functionaries inside and outside the compound, there was none who did not reverently and diligently attend to his duties. Public opinion was satisfied, to a degree that previous examinations could not match. Ah, how magnificent! On the day the thorny barriers of the examination compound were removed, forty-five scholars in all were selected. Now that the examination record has been compiled, the former Hanlin Expositor-in-Waiting Master Yu has written a detailed preface for it, and I was in turn instructed to write the postface. I have heard that scholars who set their minds on practicing the Way do not attach importance to success or failure in the examinations, but rather take the weal and woe of the people as their own concern. A former worthy said: "Literary composition suffices to adorn the person; governance can extend blessings to all things." Are these words not trustworthy indeed! At the very beginning of the Sacred Son of Heaven's succession to the throne, the refinement of selection through the examination system has reached such a level. Truly, he desires to obtain the genuine talents of the realm and employ them, so that their blessings may reach the living people and their fragrant reputation may flow down to future generations—how could this merely be a petty search to fill posts for a single moment? All you gentlemen have mastered the Classics while awaiting employment; how fortunate you are to be included in this selection! You should take the ancients as your models, using learning that illuminates fundamental principles and meets practical needs to render service to the age. Cause the people of the realm to be moistened by its blessings, so that later generations will say that for literary composition and governance, one must look to the scholars of the examinations—would that not be grand? Be diligent in this!
Written as a postface in the last ten days of the eighth month in the autumn of the first year of the Xuande era (September 1426) by Shao Siwu 邵思廡 of Kuaiji 會稽.

title: 宣德元年福建鄉試錄
text:
第一場
四書義
唐虞之際於斯為盛
辟如天地之無不持載無不覆幬辟如四時之錯行如日
月之代明萬物並育而不相害道並行而不相悖小德
川流大德敦化此天地之所以為大也
至誠而不動者未之有也不誠未有能動者也
易
元者善之長也亨者嘉之會也利者義之和也貞者事
===
之幹也君子體仁足以長人嘉會足以合禮利物足以
和義貞固足以幹事君子行此四德者故曰乾元
亨利貞
直其正也方其義也君子敬以直内義以方外敬義
立而德不孤
觀變於陰陽而立卦發揮於剛柔而生爻和順於道德
而理於義窮理盡性以至於命
聖人立象以盡意設卦以盡情偽繫辭焉以盡其言變
而通之以盡利鼓之舞之以盡神
punctuated:
第一場

四書義
唐虞之際，於斯為盛。
辟如天地之無不持載，無不覆幬；辟如四時之錯行，如日月之代明。萬物並育而不相害，道並行而不相悖。小德川流，大德敦化，此天地之所以為大也。
至誠而不動者，未之有也；不誠，未有能動者也。

易
元者，善之長也；亨者，嘉之會也；利者，義之和也；貞者，事之幹也。君子體仁足以長人，嘉會足以合禮，利物足以和義，貞固足以幹事。君子行此四德者，故曰：「乾：元、亨、利、貞。」
直其正也，方其義也。君子敬以直内，義以方外，敬義立而德不孤。
觀變於陰陽而立卦，發揮於剛柔而生爻，和順於道德而理於義，窮理盡性以至於命。
聖人立象以盡意，設卦以盡情偽，繫辭焉以盡其言，變而通之以盡利，鼓之舞之以盡神。
translation_en:
First Session

Expositions on the Four Books

"[Talent is difficult to find; is that not so?] At the juncture of Tang and Yu, it was more abundant than in this era." (Analects 8.20)

"He may be compared to Heaven and Earth in their supporting and containing all things, and their overshadowing and covering all things. He may be compared to the four seasons in their alternating progress, and to the sun and moon in their successive shining. All things are nourished together without their injuring one another; the courses of the seasons and the sun and moon are pursued without any collision among them. The smaller energies are like river currents; the greater energies are seen in mighty transformations. It is this that makes Heaven and Earth so great!" (Doctrine of the Mean 30)

"Never has there been one possessed of complete sincerity who did not move others. Never has there been one without sincerity who was able to move others." (Mencius 4A.12)

Book of Changes (Yijing)

"'Originating' (yuan) is the chief of all goodness; 'penetrating' (heng) is the assemblage of excellences; 'advantageous' (li) is the harmony of all righteousness; 'correct and firm' (zhen) is the stem of all affairs. The noble man, embodying benevolence, is fit to preside over men; bringing together excellences, he is fit to show a conformity to ritual propriety; benefitting all creatures, he is fit to exhibit the harmony of righteousness; correct and firm, he is fit to manage affairs. Because the noble man practices these four virtues, it is said: 'Qian: originating, penetrating, advantageous, correct and firm.'" (Qian, Wenyan commentary)

"'Straight' indicates the correctness of the internal principle; 'square' indicates the righteousness of the external act. The noble man uses reverence to straighten the internal life and righteousness to square the external world. When reverence and righteousness are established, his virtue is not solitary." (Kun, Wenyan commentary)

"[In the past, when the sages made the Changes,] they observed the transformations of yin and yang and established the trigrams; they brought into play the firm and the yielding and produced the lines; they harmonized with the Way and its virtue and ordered things according to righteousness; they exhausted the principles of things and fulfilled their natures, thereby arriving at an understanding of destiny." (Shuo gua 1)

"The sages established the images in order to express their ideas fully; they set up the hexagrams in order to treat the true and the false fully; they appended the explanations in order to express their words fully; they changed and generalized them in order to achieve the full benefit; they drummed and danced them in order to exhaust the spiritual." (Xi ci A.12)

title: 宣德元年福建鄉試錄
text:
書
詢于四岳闢四門明四目達四聰咨十有二牧曰食哉惟時
其難其慎惟和惟一
四五紀一曰歲二曰月三曰日四曰星辰五曰曆數
自古商人亦越我周文王立政立事牧夫準人則克宅之
克由繹之茲乃俾乂
詩
篤公劉逝彼百泉瞻彼溥原廼陟南岡乃覯于京京
師之野于時處處于時廬旅于時言言于時語語
===
作召公考天子萬壽
載見辟王曰求厥章龍旂陽陽和鈴央央鞗革有鶴
休有烈光率見昭考以孝以享以介眉壽永言保
之思皇多祜
自天降康豐年穰穰來假來饗降福無疆顧予烝嘗
湯孫之將
春秋
諸侯盟于首止〔僖公五年〕諸侯盟于葵丘〔僖公九年〕同盟于柯
陵〔成公十七年〕同盟于鷄澤〔襄公三年〕同盟于平丘〔昭公十三年〕
punctuated:
書：
詢于四岳，闢四門，明四目，達四聰。咨十有二牧，曰：「食哉惟時。」
其難其慎，惟和惟一。
四、五紀：一曰歲，二曰月，三曰日，四曰星辰，五曰曆數。
自古商人，亦越我周文王，立政立事、牧夫、準人，則克宅之，克由繹之，茲乃俾乂。

詩：
篤公劉，逝彼百泉，瞻彼溥原；廼陟南岡，乃覯于京。京師之野，于時處處，于時廬旅，于時言言，于時語語。
作召公考，天子萬壽。
載見辟王，曰求厥章。龍旂陽陽，和鈴央央，鞗革有鶴，休有烈光。率見昭考，以孝以享，以介眉壽。永言保之，思皇多祜。
自天降康，豐年穰穰。來假來饗，降福無疆。顧予烝嘗，湯孫之將。

春秋：
諸侯盟于首止〔僖公五年〕，諸侯盟于葵丘〔僖公九年〕，同盟于柯陵〔成公十七年〕，同盟于鷄澤〔襄公三年〕，同盟于平丘〔昭公十三年〕。
translation_en:
Document Classic (Shu):
He deliberated with the Four Peaks, threw open the four gates, saw with the eyes of all in the four quarters, and heard with the ears of all in the four quarters. He consulted the Twelve Pastors, saying, "Food—this depends on observing the seasons!"
How difficult it is! How cautious you must be! Be harmonious; be of one mind.
Fourth, the Five Regulators: the first is called the year, the second is called the month, the third is called the day, the fourth is called the stars and zodiacal spaces, and the fifth is called the calendrical calculations.
From antiquity, the men of Shang, as well as our King Wen of Zhou, in establishing government and appointing functionaries, pastors, and keepers of the law, were able to place the right men in office and draw out their abilities; thus they entrusted them with governance.

Poetry Classic (Shi):
Staunch was Duke Liu; he went to those Hundred Springs and gazed upon that vast plain; then he ascended the southern ridge and looked upon the great hill. A wild fit for a capital city: here he dwelt in his residence, here he lodged his guests, here he spoke out, here he conversed.
You have achieved success, Duke of Shao; may the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years!
They appeared before their sovereign king to seek their emblems of rank. Their dragon-banners blazed brightly, their carriage-bells and banner-bells rang clear, their ornamented reins gleamed, and glorious was their resplendent majesty. He led them to appear before the shrine of his glorious father, to show filial piety, to present offerings, and to increase longevity with bushy eyebrows. Forever may they preserve it; truly great and abundant are the blessings.
From Heaven comes down prosperity, and years of abundance in rich measure. Come, approach; come, enjoy the offerings, and send down blessings without limit. Regard our winter and autumn sacrifices, presented by the descendant of Tang.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):
The feudal lords made a covenant at Shouzhi [fifth year of Duke Xi]; the feudal lords made a covenant at Kuiqiu [ninth year of Duke Xi]; they joined in a covenant at Keling [seventeenth year of Duke Cheng]; they joined in a covenant at Jize [third year of Duke Xiang]; they joined in a covenant at Pingqiu [thirteenth year of Duke Zhao].

title: 宣德元年福建鄉試錄
text:
齊侯宋人陳人蔡人邾人會于北杏莊公十三年公會齊侯
宋公陳侯鄭伯同盟于幽莊公二十七年
遂伐楚公至自伐楚僖公四年公會齊侯于夾谷公
至自夾谷定公十年
公會晋侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭伯衛子莒子盟于踐土公
朝于王所僖公二十八年公會晋侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭
伯陳子莒子邾子秦人于溫天王狩于河陽壬申
公朝于王所同年
禮記
===
是故聖人之記事也慮之以大愛之以敬行之以禮脩
之以孝養紀之以義終之以仁是故古之人一舉事
而衆皆知其德之備也
是故夫政必本於天殽以降命命降于社之謂殽地降
于祖廟之謂仁義降於山川之謂興作降於五祀
之謂制度
古之聖人內之爲尊外之爲樂少之爲貴多之爲美是
故先王之制禮也不可多也不可寡也唯其稱也
夫歌者直己而陳德也動己而天地應焉四時和焉星辰
punctuated:
齊侯、宋人、陳人、蔡人、邾人會于北杏。莊公十三年。公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、鄭伯同盟于幽。莊公二十七年。
遂伐楚，公至自伐楚。僖公四年。公會齊侯于夾谷，公至自夾谷。定公十年。
公會晋侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、衛子、莒子盟于踐土，公朝于王所。僖公二十八年。公會晋侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、陳子、莒子、邾子、秦人于溫，天王狩于河陽，壬申，公朝于王所。同年。
《禮記》
是故聖人之記事也，慮之以大，愛之以敬，行之以禮，脩之以孝養，紀之以義，終之以仁。是故古之人一舉事，而衆皆知其德之備也。
是故夫政必本於天，殽以降命。命降于社之謂殽地，降于祖廟之謂仁義，降於山川之謂興作，降於五祀之謂制度。
古之聖人，內之爲尊，外之爲樂；少之爲貴，多之爲美。是故先王之制禮也，不可多也，不可寡也，唯其稱也。
夫歌者，直己而陳德也。動己而天地應焉，四時和焉，星辰
translation_en:
“The Marquis of Qi, a man of Song, a man of Chen, a man of Cai, and a man of Zhu met at Beixing.” (13th year of Duke Zhuang.) “The Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, and the Earl of Zheng, and together they made a covenant at You.” (27th year of Duke Zhuang.)
“They thereupon attacked Chu. The Duke arrived back from attacking Chu.” (4th year of Duke Xi.) “The Duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The Duke arrived back from Jiagu.” (10th year of Duke Ding.)
“The Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Wei, and the Viscount of Ju, and made a covenant at Jiantu. The Duke had an audience at the King’s place.” (28th year of Duke Xi.) “The Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Chen, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, and a man of Qin at Wen. The Heavenly King hunted at Heyang. On the renshen day, the Duke had an audience at the King’s place.” (The same year.)
Record of Rites (Liji)
“Therefore, when the sage records affairs, he contemplates them with greatness, cherishes them with reverence, conducts them with ritual propriety, cultivates them with filial nourishment, regulates them with righteousness, and completes them with benevolence. Therefore, when the ancients undertook a single affair, the multitude all knew the perfection of their virtue.”
“Therefore, governance must be rooted in Heaven, imitating it to send down commands. When commands descend at the altar of the soil, it is called imitating the earth; when they descend at the ancestral temple, it is called benevolence and righteousness; when they descend at the mountains and rivers, it is called initiating works; when they descend at the five household sacrifices, it is called institutional regulations.”
“The sages of antiquity took what was internal as venerable and what was external as joyful; they took fewness as noble and abundance as admirable. Therefore, when the former kings instituted rites, they could neither be too many nor too few, but only what was fitting.”
“Now singing is straightening oneself and setting forth virtue. One moves oneself, and Heaven and Earth respond to it, the four seasons are harmonized by it, the stars and constellations…”

問：伏讀太祖高皇帝《御製大誥》序文有曰：「立綱陳紀，為民造福。」又曰：「君

title: 宣德元年福建鄉試錄
text:
臣同心志同一氣大哉
皇言乎自國初以来餘六十年其間居廟堂司風紀職方面任守
令能同心一志為民造福者蓋可見矣其治效可以
比隆於唐虞三代歟
太宗文皇帝頒為善陰隲書于天下所載范仲淹之經濟趙抃之
讞疑富弼之救灾蘇軾之惠愛其政蹟可得聞歟諸士
子蒙樂育之久負明體適用之學今兹賓興駸駸嚮
用他日或居廟堂或司風紀或職方面或任守令亦
有志古人之所志而為民造福于將来者歟請試言
===
之以觀所蘊
問六經所以明聖道也易以明陰陽書以道政事詩以理
性情禮以制事樂以和心春秋以正名分豈各有所專
而不相通歟說者謂一經之內諸經之理無不該謂洪範
書之易也賡歌書之詩也伯夷典禮后夔典樂書之禮
樂也命德討罪書之春秋也其義果相貫歟又謂春秋
之義公好惡則發乎詩之情酌古今則貫乎書之事與
常典則體乎禮之序本忠恕則導乎樂之和亦可指其
一二以實之歟若易詩禮三經之中亦必有可貫諸經
punctuated:
臣同心，志同一氣。」大哉，皇言乎！自國初以来餘六十年，其間居廟堂、司風紀、職方面、任守令，能同心一志，為民造福者，蓋可見矣。其治效可以比隆於唐虞三代歟？太宗文皇帝頒《為善陰隲書》于天下，所載范仲淹之經濟、趙抃之讞疑、富弼之救灾、蘇軾之惠愛，其政蹟可得聞歟？諸士子蒙樂育之久，負明體適用之學，今兹賓興，駸駸嚮用。他日或居廟堂，或司風紀，或職方面，或任守令，亦有志古人之所志，而為民造福于將来者歟？請試言之，以觀所蘊。

問：六經所以明聖道也。《易》以明陰陽，《書》以道政事，《詩》以理性情，《禮》以制事，《樂》以和心，《春秋》以正名分，豈各有所專而不相通歟？說者謂一經之內，諸經之理無不該，謂《洪範》，《書》之《易》也；《賡歌》，《書》之《詩》也；伯夷典禮，后夔典樂，《書》之《禮》《樂》也；命德討罪，《書》之《春秋》也。其義果相貫歟？又謂《春秋》之義，公好惡則發乎《詩》之情，酌古今則貫乎《書》之事，與常典則體乎《禮》之序，本忠恕則導乎《樂》之和，亦可指其一二以實之歟？若《易》《詩》《禮》三經之中，亦必有可貫諸經
translation_en:
…ministers are of one mind, their purposes united in a single spirit.” How great are these imperial words! In the more than sixty years since the dynasty’s founding, there have surely been men serving at court, overseeing official discipline, holding regional responsibilities, or serving as prefects and magistrates who united in mind and purpose to bring blessings to the people. Could their achievements in government rival the flourishing rule of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties? Emperor Taizong Wen promulgated throughout the realm the Book of Doing Good and Hidden Blessings (Weishan yinzhi shu). May we hear about the administrative achievements recorded there: Fan Zhongyan’s statecraft, Zhao Bian’s adjudication of doubtful cases, Fu Bi’s disaster relief, and Su Shi’s benevolent care? You candidates have long enjoyed nurturing instruction and possess learning that illuminates fundamental principles and applies them to practical affairs. Now, honored and recommended through this examination, you are steadily approaching appointment to office. When you one day serve at court, oversee official discipline, hold regional responsibilities, or serve as prefects and magistrates, will you also aspire to what the ancients aspired to and bring blessings to the people in years to come? Please set forth your views, so that we may discern what you have within you.

Question: The Six Classics illuminate the Way of the sages. The Changes elucidates yin and yang; the Documents expounds affairs of government; the Odes orders human nature and feelings; the Rites regulates conduct; the Music harmonizes the heart; and the Spring and Autumn Annals rectifies names and social distinctions. Does each specialize in something without communicating with the others? Commentators say that within any one classic, all the principles of the other classics are encompassed. They say that the “Great Plan” is the Changes within the Documents; the “Responsive Songs” is the Odes within the Documents; Bo Yi’s direction of ritual and Hou Kui’s direction of music are the Rites and Music within the Documents; and the appointment of the virtuous and punishment of the guilty are the Spring and Autumn Annals within the Documents. Are their meanings indeed interconnected? They also say that, in the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals, impartiality in approval and disapproval springs from the feelings expressed in the Odes; weighing past and present connects with the affairs recorded in the Documents; upholding constant norms [?] embodies the order of the Rites; and taking loyalty and reciprocity as the foundation leads to the harmony of the Music. Can you point to one or two examples to substantiate this? Within the three classics—the Changes, the Odes, and the Rites—there must likewise be something that connects the various classics…

title: 宣德元年福建鄉試錄
text:
之義者願悉陳之以見諸士子貫通之學
問稽往行摭前聞學者之事也漢之董仲舒賈誼鄭玄劉
向皆鉅儒也後世唯稱賈董而鄭劉不與焉玄之疏九
經亦勞矣向之諫疏懇切而亦有著述何以不並稱於
賈董歟唐之初河汾王氏爲學者所宗所著書曰文中
子韓子後出能著原道闢異端二子之優劣可得而論
歟宋之周夫子二程夫子倡明道學若横渠之晚變至道邵
康節之理數司馬温公之上無師傅其有合於周程者
果何在歟南宋諸儒唯朱子爲得其宗若當時稱陸
===
子靜為臨川之學呂成公為金華之學張南軒為廣
漢之學與朱子之論道有異同者可得而指其槩歟
願悉陳之毋泛毋略
問昔之爲治者莫不重農事以足民食若戰国時魏之李悝
作盡地力之教西漢趙充國罷騎兵屯田於西邊使兵
旅不坐食而民省輸轉之役其法制之立皆可得而聞
歟唐開元中置屯隸司農其給牛有軟地硬地之分者何
歟先儒謂其可以周時下農夫為率一夫可食五人又
何以見之歟今屯田之兵散布於中夏而偏毗於邊
punctuated:
之義者，願悉陳之，以見諸士子貫通之學。

問：稽往行、摭前聞，學者之事也。漢之董仲舒、賈誼、鄭玄、劉向，皆鉅儒也。後世唯稱賈、董，而鄭、劉不與焉。玄之疏九經，亦勞矣；向之諫疏懇切，而亦有著述，何以不並稱於賈、董歟？唐之初，河汾王氏爲學者所宗，所著書曰《文中子》；韓子後出，能著《原道》，闢異端。二子之優劣，可得而論歟？宋之周夫子、二程夫子倡明道學，若横渠之晚變至道、邵康節之理數、司馬温公之上無師傅，其有合於周、程者，果何在歟？南宋諸儒，唯朱子爲得其宗。若當時稱陸子靜為臨川之學，呂成公為金華之學，張南軒為廣漢之學，與朱子之論道有異同者，可得而指其槩歟？願悉陳之，毋泛毋略。

問：昔之爲治者，莫不重農事以足民食。若戰国時魏之李悝作盡地力之教，西漢趙充國罷騎兵屯田於西邊，使兵旅不坐食，而民省輸轉之役，其法制之立，皆可得而聞歟？唐開元中，置屯隸司農，其給牛有軟地、硬地之分者，何歟？先儒謂其可以周時下農夫為率，一夫可食五人，又何以見之歟？今屯田之兵，散布於中夏而偏毗於邊
translation_en:
… principles of the other Classics; please set them forth in full, so as to demonstrate the gentlemen's comprehensive learning.

Question: Examining past conduct and gathering records of what was previously heard is the business of scholars. In the Han dynasty, Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒, Jia Yi 賈誼, Zheng Xuan 鄭玄, and Liu Xiang 劉向 were all great Confucians. Yet later generations praised only Jia and Dong, without including Zheng and Liu. Zheng Xuan's commentaries on the Nine Classics were certainly laborious, and Liu Xiang's remonstrance memorials were earnest and sincere, besides which he also authored works of his own—why then were they notranked alongside Jia and Dong? At the beginning of the Tang dynasty, Master Wang of Hefen 河汾 (Wang Tong 王通) was revered as an authority by scholars, and the book he wrote was called the Master Wenzhong (Wenzhongzi 文中子); Master Han (Han Yu 韓愈) appeared later and was able to write "Tracing the Way" (Yuandao 原道) and refute heterodoxies. Can the relative merits of these two masters be discussed? In the Song dynasty, Master Zhou (Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤) and the two Masters Cheng (Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤) championed and illuminated the Learning of the Way (Daoxue 道學). As for Zhang Zai 張載 (Hengqu 横渠) transforming in his later years to reach the Supreme Way, Shao Yong 邵雍 (Shao Kangjie 邵康節) with his principle and number, and Sima Guang 司馬光 (Sima Wengong 司馬温公) who had no teacher above him—wherein did their agreement with Zhou and the Chengs truly lie? Among the scholars of the Southern Song, Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹) alone grasped the true lineage. As for those spoken of at the time—Lu Jiuyuan 陸九淵 (Lu Zijing 陸子靜) as the school of Linchuan 臨川, Lü Zuqian 呂祖謙 (Lü Chenggong 呂成公) as the school of Jinhua 金華, and Zhang Shi 張栻 (Zhang Nanxuan 張南軒) as the school of Guanghan 廣漢—can the general outlines of their similarities and differences with Master Zhu in discussing the Way be pointed out? Please set them forth in full, without being vague or cursory.

Question: Those who governed in antiquity never failed to emphasize agriculture in order to make the people's food sufficient. In the Warring States period, Li Kui 李悝 of Wei 魏 created the teaching on exhausting the strength of the soil, and in the Western Han, Zhao Chongguo 趙充國 disbanded cavalrymen to establish state farms (tuntian 屯田) on the western frontier, so that the troops did not sit idle eating rations and the common people were spared the labor of transport. Can the establishment of their systems and regulations all be recounted? During the Kaiyuan 開元 era (713–741) of the Tang, state farms were established under the Court of Imperial Granaries (Sinong 司農); why was the allocation of oxen divided according to soft land and hard land? Earlier scholars said that this could be measured by the standard of a lower-grade farmer in Zhou times, whereby one man could feed five people—how can this be seen? Today, soldiers on state farms are scattered throughout the central lands and concentrated along the frontier …

title: 宣德元年福建鄉試錄
text:
徵亦有足於兵餉而省於轉輸歟願聞其說
問作樂必審於律呂不審律呂則樂不和昔軒轅命伶倫
取嶰谷之竹製為十二管果何所取義歟至漢京房又
為六十律果得其當歟若黃鍾圍徑之數寸以九分為
法五聲二變之數半律半聲之例變宮變徵之不得為
調又可得而知其詳歟至宋竇儼王朴初定周樂繼
以和峴所定則下王朴一律又繼以李照所定則下王朴
三律果孰是而孰非歟議者謂朴之所知者音照之所
知者器音之與器同歟異歟其亦有淺深歟自是而
===
後有知律呂制作之詳者亦有其人歟願聞其說
punctuated:
徵，亦有足於兵餉而省於轉輸歟？願聞其說。
問：作樂必審於律呂，不審律呂則樂不和。昔軒轅命伶倫取嶰谷之竹，製為十二管，果何所取義歟？至漢京房，又為六十律，果得其當歟？若黃鍾圍徑之數，寸以九分為法，五聲二變之數，半律半聲之例，變宮變徵之不得為調，又可得而知其詳歟？至宋竇儼、王朴初定周樂，繼以和峴所定，則下王朴一律；又繼以李照所定，則下王朴三律，果孰是而孰非歟？議者謂朴之所知者音，照之所知者器，音之與器，同歟？異歟？其亦有淺深歟？自是而後，有知律呂制作之詳者，亦有其人歟？願聞其說。
translation_en:
…frontiers [reading 徵 as 徼?]; is this also sufficient to supply military provisions and save on transport labor? I wish to hear your explanation of this.

Question: In creating music, one must carefully examine the standard pitch-pipes (lülü); if the pitch-pipes are not carefully examined, the music will not be harmonious. In antiquity, Xuanyuan [the Yellow Emperor] ordered Ling Lun to take bamboo from Xie Valley and fashion it into twelve pipes—what meaning was truly drawn from this? By the Han dynasty, Jing Fang further created sixty pitches—did he truly achieve what was proper? As for the numbers of the circumference and diameter of the Yellow Bell (huangzhong) pipe, the rule of dividing the inch into nine parts, the numbers of the five tones and two altered tones, the principles of half-pitches and half-tones, and why the altered gong (biangong) and altered zhi (bianzhi) cannot serve as modes—can the details of these also be known? Coming to the Song dynasty, Dou Yan and Wang Pu first established the music of the Later Zhou; subsequently, what He Xian established was one pitch lower than Wang Pu's, and after that, what Li Zhao established was three pitches lower than Wang Pu's—which of these was truly right and which wrong? Commentators say that what Pu understood was musical sound (yin), whereas what Zhao understood was musical instruments (qi). Are sound and instruments the same or different? Is there also a difference in depth between them? From that time onward, have there been individuals who understood the details of making the pitch-pipes? I wish to hear your explanation of this.
